message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide to **public / commercial APIs** that accept an IPv4/IPv6 address and return “company”‑level metadata—including domain ownership, registrant name, email addresses, phone numbers, and sometimes even social links—when those records exist in public WHOIS/TLD databases or proprietary business directories. | Service | Key Features | Typical Response Fields | Free Tier | Notes | |---------|--------------|------------------------|-----------|-------| | **ipinfo.io** | • Country + city
• Organization & ASN
• Company name/email/phone (if registered)
• Carrier | `org`, `hostname`, `city`, `region`, `country`, `postal`, `timezone`, `latitude`, `longitude`
`company.name`, `company.domain`, `company.email`, `company.phone` | Yes – up to ~50k/month | Requires API key (`?token=…`). Good balance between depth and cost ($9/mo). | | **ipdata.co** | • ISP, organization, AS
• Business owner/contact
• Domain registration info | `organization_name`, `asn`, `isp`, `domain_owner_email`, `domain_phone_number`, `business_address` | Yes – up to 500 req/day | Token-based auth. Offers a generous free tier but rate limits apply. | | **ipwho.is** | • City/country
• Org + ASN
• Contact emails (via WHOIS lookup) | `network.org`, `network.asn`, `as.owner`, `email`, `name`, `address` | Unlimited (but limited to 10 req/minute) | No API key needed; simple JSON endpoint. | | **MaxMind GeoLite2 + WhoisDB** | • Precise geolocation
• WHOIS record extraction (requires separate DB) | Custom schema based on whois data | Free (GeoLite2); Paid for WhoIsDB | You host it yourself → full control, no per-request costs. | | **DomainTools API** | • Full WHOIS history
• Registrant contacts, admin, tech, billing emails/phones
• DNS zone transfer status | `registrar`, `creation_date`, `expiration_date`, `nameservers[]`, `contact.admin.email`, `contact.tech.email`, … | Trial only | Enterprise‑grade; best when you already have a domain list. | --- ### How to Call One of These Services #### Example: Using *ipinfo.io* (Python) ```python import requests API_TOKEN = "" BASE_URL = f"https://ipinfo.io/{'8.8.8.8'}" resp = requests.get(BASE_URL, params={"token": API_TOKEN}) data = resp.json() print("Organization:", data.get('org')) print("Company Name :", data.get('company', {}).get('name')) print("Email :", data.get('company', {}).get('email')) ``` Sample Output: ```json { "ip":"8.8.8.8", "hostname":"dns.google", "anycast":true, "reverse_dns":"dns.google", "category":"ISP", "continent_code":"NA", "continent_name":"North America", "country_iso_code":"US", "country_name":"United States", "location":{ "lat":37.751,"lon":-97.822}, "org":"AS15169 Google LLC", "postal":"94035", "region":"California", "timezone":"America/Los_Angeles", "company":{ "name":"Google Inc.", "domain":"google.com", "email":"support@google.com", "phone":"+1-650-253-0000"} } ``` If the IP belongs to a private network or a non‑registered entity, many of the optional fields (`company.*`) will simply be omitted. #### Quick CURL Alternative ```bash curl -s "https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8?token=$IPINFO_TOKEN" | jq . ``` Replace `$IPINFO_TOKEN` with your actual token. --- ### Choosing the Right Provider | Use Case | Recommended Service(s) | |----------|------------------------| | **Lightweight lookups (<10k/month)** | `ipwho.is` (free) or `ipinfo.io` (basic plan) | | **Need corporate contact details** | `ipdata.co` or `ipinfo.io` premium | | **Enterprise integration, bulk queries** | `DomainTools` or self-hosted `MaxMind` + custom WHOIS parser | | **Compliance / GDPR** | Verify provider’s data retention policy; consider local hosting (e.g., MaxMind) so raw WHOIS isn’t transmitted externally | --- ### Caveats & Best Practices 1. **Rate Limits:** Most free plans throttle at ~10–20 QPS. For higher throughput, upgrade or batch requests. 2. **Privacy Laws:** Some jurisdictions restrict publishing personal contact info extracted from WHOIS. Ensure compliance before exposing data downstream. 3. **Data Freshness:** WHOIS updates lag behind real changes. Cache results where possible. 4. **Error Handling:** Always check `status` field or HTTP status code; missing keys mean “no data”. 5. **Caching Strategy:** Store successful lookups keyed by IP for at least 24h to reduce repeated external traffic. --- ### Next Steps 1. Sign up for one of the above providers and grab an API key/token. 2. Pick a programming language/library you’re comfortable with (requests in Python, axios in Node.js, fetch in Go). 3. Wrap the call in a small helper module that normalizes the varying schemas across providers into a single internal structure: ```ts interface IpInfo { ip: string; org?: string; companyName?: string; companyEmail?: string; companyPhone?: string; } ``` 4. Add caching (Redis/LRU) and error logging. 5. Deploy behind your existing microservice layer or expose as a lightweight REST endpoint. Happy coding! Let me know if you'd like deeper dives into any particular provider or help wiring this into your stack.
